definition: Classification B supplies concrete and abstract predicates on the candidate domain together with required disjointness (∀ x, abstract x → ¬ concrete x). Neither predicate is defined as the complement of the other, and nothing forces every candidate into one of them: borderline or unclassified candidates are permitted. Concreteness is world-independent; concreteness at a world (ConcreteAt) is existence there together with concreteness.
note: Shared typed vocabulary for #1103, replacing ad-hoc free concrete parameters where the meaning coincides. The adopted sense is DEF-CONCRETE-ESSE-IN-RE; rival criteria are sibling senses under DISAMB-CONCRETE-ABSTRACT-CRITERIA.
